# CLI scenario transcripts

Generated by `go run ./internal/tools/scenario doc -write internal/scenario/testdata/transcripts.md`;
`go test ./internal/scenario` fails when this file is stale. Do not edit by hand.

**Scenario mode.** Every transcript below comes from running the real
`purlview` command handlers in-process against controlled fixtures: a fake
platform, fake sign-in, a fake target probe, fake release metadata and an
in-process daemon built on the real share engine, all on a fake clock.
Recipient scenarios also model host-only cookie jars, verification mail,
upstream requests and active streams against that same platform authority.
All tokens are visibly synthetic and deterministic, not cryptographic proof.
Access follows separate entry and content domains with single-use handoffs,
and a recipient may reach the whole origin of a share; `purlview logout`
signs this device out locally. The recipient model is not a browser: real
browser isolation and the service's own enforcement are outside these
scenarios, and link scanners are not modelled.
Identities and domains are synthetic (`example.invalid`, `purlview.invalid`).
Nothing contacts a real service, opens a real browser or touches your own
daemon. A transcript demonstrates the intended command behaviour and the
contract it needs; it does not prove process or socket guarantees, which
the daemon lifecycle tests cover.

**Reading a transcript.** `$` is the command line; `stdout|` and `stderr|`
tag each output line with its stream; `--` lines are fixture actions (a
lost connection, a clock advance, Ctrl-C); `= exit N` is the exit status.
When a second command runs while a foreground share is still attached, the
share's later lines appear after that command under a "continued" heading.
The fake clock starts at 2026-09-16 12:00:00 UTC and only moves when a
scenario advances it, so an hour of expiry costs no test time.

## First use

### first-use/interactive-share-signs-in

An interactive first share signs the user in with an email code, then shares.

Fixtures: signed out; interactive terminal; an email code is verified.

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000
stderr|
stderr| Sign in to Purlview
stderr|
stderr|   Email:
stderr|   Code sent. Check your inbox.
stderr|   Code:
stderr|
stderr| ✓ Signed in as creator@example.invalid
stderr|
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     Ctrl-C
        -- clock +1h
stderr|
stderr| 1:00 PM  ! Expires in 5 minutes
stderr| 1:00 PM  Share expired
= exit 0
```

### first-use/existing-identity-skips-sign-in

A signed-in installation shares without any sign-in step.

Fixtures: signed in as the creator on this device.

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000 --background
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     purlview stop k7m2p4qx
= exit 0
$ purlview whoami
stdout| Account  creator@example.invalid
stdout| Device   studio
stdout| Status   Signed in
= exit 0
```

### first-use/noninteractive-unauthenticated

Without a terminal, a share that is not signed in says how to sign in and asks nothing.

Fixtures: signed out; standard input and error are not terminals (a script or a pipe).

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000 --background
stderr| ✗ Not signed in — run purlview login first
= exit 1
$ purlview list
stderr| ✗ Not signed in — run purlview login first
= exit 1
```

## Login

### login/email-code

login asks for the email address and the emailed 6-digit code, typed as hidden text, and ends at the signed-in line.

Fixtures: signed out; an email code arrives.

```text
$ purlview login
stderr|
stderr| Sign in to Purlview
stderr|
stderr|   Email:
        -- the user types: creator@example.invalid
stderr|   Code sent. Check your inbox.
stderr|   Code:
        -- the user types, unseen: ·······
stderr|
stderr| ✓ Signed in as creator@example.invalid
= exit 0
$ purlview whoami
stdout| Account  creator@example.invalid
stdout| Device   studio
stdout| Status   Signed in
= exit 0
```

### login/wrong-code

A wrong code asks again with the attempts left; the fifth miss ends the sign-in (exit 1).

Fixtures: signed out; the user mistypes the code.

```text
$ purlview login
stderr|
stderr| Sign in to Purlview
stderr|
stderr|   Email:
        -- the user types: creator@example.invalid
stderr|   Code sent. Check your inbox.
stderr|   Code:
        -- the user types, unseen: ······
stderr| ✗ That code didn't match — 4 attempts left
stderr|   Code:
        -- the user types, unseen: ·····
stderr| ✗ That code didn't match — codes have 6 digits
stderr|   Code:
        -- the user types, unseen: ······
stderr|
stderr| ✓ Signed in as creator@example.invalid
= exit 0
$ purlview logout
stderr| ✓ Signed out on this device — running shares continue until stopped or expired
= exit 0
$ purlview login
stderr|
stderr| Sign in to Purlview
stderr|
stderr|   Email:
        -- the user types: creator@example.invalid
stderr|   Code sent. Check your inbox.
stderr|   Code:
        -- the user types, unseen: ······
stderr| ✗ That code didn't match — 4 attempts left
stderr|   Code:
        -- the user types, unseen: ······
stderr| ✗ That code didn't match — 3 attempts left
stderr|   Code:
        -- the user types, unseen: ······
stderr| ✗ That code didn't match — 2 attempts left
stderr|   Code:
        -- the user types, unseen: ······
stderr| ✗ That code didn't match — 1 attempt left
stderr|   Code:
        -- the user types, unseen: ······
stderr| ✗ That code has expired — run purlview login to get a new one
= exit 1
```

### login/resend-code

Typing resend sends a new code after a minute, twice per sign-in; asking earlier says how long to wait.

Fixtures: signed out; the first email never arrives.

```text
$ purlview login
stderr|
stderr| Sign in to Purlview
stderr|
stderr|   Email:
        -- the user types: creator@example.invalid
stderr|   Code sent. Check your inbox.
stderr|   Code:
        -- clock +20s
        -- the user types, unseen: resend
stderr| ! Wait 40s before asking for another code
stderr|   Code:
        -- clock +40s
        -- the user types, unseen: resend
stderr|   Code sent. Check your inbox.
stderr|   Code:
        -- clock +1m
        -- the user types, unseen: resend
stderr|   Code sent. Check your inbox.
stderr|   Code:
        -- clock +1m
        -- the user types, unseen: resend
stderr| ! No more codes for this sign-in — run purlview login to start over
stderr|   Code:
        -- the user types, unseen: ······
stderr|
stderr| ✓ Signed in as creator@example.invalid
= exit 0
```

Without a terminal, login reads the email address and the code as two lines of standard input.

```text
stderr|

stderr|   Code:
stderr|
```

### login/no-browser-flag-rejected

--no-browser is not a login flag; it is rejected before sign-in.

Fixtures: signed out.

```text
$ purlview login --no-browser
stderr| ✗ Unknown flag: --no-browser
stderr| Run 'purlview login --help' for usage.
= exit 2
```

### login/cancelled

Ctrl-C at a prompt ends its line, prints nothing more and exits 130.

Fixtures: signed out; the user presses Ctrl-C at the code prompt.

```text
$ purlview login
stderr|
stderr| Sign in to Purlview
stderr|
stderr|   Email:
        -- the user types: creator@example.invalid
stderr|   Code sent. Check your inbox.
stderr|   Code:
        -- Ctrl-C
= exit 130
```

### login/timeout

A code that is never entered expires after five minutes (exit 1).

Fixtures: signed out; no code is entered; the fake clock passes the five-minute lifetime.

```text
$ purlview login
stderr|
stderr| Sign in to Purlview
stderr|
stderr|   Email:
        -- the user types: creator@example.invalid
stderr|   Code sent. Check your inbox.
stderr|   Code:
        -- clock advances (1m steps) until: has expired
stderr| ✗ That code has expired — run purlview login to get a new one
= exit 1
```

### login/repeated-and-signed-out-elsewhere

A repeated login confirms who is signed in; only a device that was signed out signs in again.

Fixtures: signed in; later, this device is signed out from the console.

```text
$ purlview login
stderr| ✓ Signed in as creator@example.invalid
= exit 0
        -- this device is signed out from the console
$ purlview login
stderr| ! This device was signed out — sign in again
stderr|
stderr| Sign in to Purlview
stderr|
stderr|   Email:
stderr|   Code sent. Check your inbox.
stderr|   Code:
stderr|
stderr| ✓ Signed in as creator@example.invalid
= exit 0
```

### login/credential-save-fails

When the sign-in cannot be saved on this device, login says whether Purlview still lists the device.

Fixtures: signed out; the credential store refuses to save; the second attempt happens while the platform is unreachable.

```text
$ purlview login
stderr|
stderr| Sign in to Purlview
stderr|
stderr|   Email:
stderr|   Code sent. Check your inbox.
stderr|   Code:
stderr| ✗ Couldn't save your sign-in on this device — nothing stays signed in
= exit 1
        -- platform unreachable right after the code is accepted
$ purlview login
stderr|
stderr| Sign in to Purlview
stderr|
stderr|   Email:
stderr|   Code sent. Check your inbox.
stderr|   Code:
stderr| ✗ Couldn't save your sign-in on this device — Purlview still lists it; sign it out with purlview devices
= exit 1
```

### login/platform-unavailable

login fails clearly when Purlview cannot be reached.

Fixtures: signed out; the platform is unreachable.

```text
$ purlview login
stderr|
stderr| Sign in to Purlview
stderr|
stderr|   Email:
stderr| ✗ Couldn't reach Purlview — check your connection and try again
= exit 1
```

## Foreground share

### foreground/ready-url-and-expiry

A foreground share prints its block once the link works, warns five minutes before the end, and finishes normally at expiry.

Fixtures: signed in; localhost:3000 answers.

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     Ctrl-C
        -- clock +55m
stderr|
stderr| 12:55 PM  ! Expires in 5 minutes
        -- clock +5m
stderr| 1:00 PM  Share expired
= exit 0
```

### foreground/visitor-and-app-events

The first visitor, and an app that stops and resumes answering, each append one line with the local time.

Fixtures: signed in; a foreground share is ready; a visitor opens the app, which stops answering and recovers.

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     Ctrl-C
        -- clock +44m
        -- a visitor opens the app; the app stops answering, then answers again
stderr|
stderr| 12:44 PM  ● First visitor opened the app
stderr| 12:44 PM  ! localhost:3000 stopped responding — visitors see a waiting page
stderr| 12:44 PM  ✓ localhost:3000 is responding again
        -- Ctrl-C
stderr| 12:44 PM  ✓ Stopped — the link no longer works
= exit 0
```

### foreground/ctrl-c-stops-and-confirms

Ctrl-C ends the foreground share; success is reported only with the platform's confirmation.

Fixtures: signed in; the platform confirms the revocation.

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     Ctrl-C
        -- Ctrl-C
stderr|
stderr| 12:00 PM  ✓ Stopped — the link no longer works
= exit 0
```

### foreground/ctrl-c-while-offline-is-unconfirmed

Ctrl-C while Purlview is unreachable stops here and says by when the link stops working (exit 1).

Fixtures: signed in; the platform becomes unreachable after the share is ready.

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     Ctrl-C
        -- platform unreachable
        -- Ctrl-C
stderr|
stderr| 12:00 PM  ! Stopped here, but Purlview couldn't confirm — the link stops working by 1:00 PM
= exit 1
```

### foreground/cli-killed-ends-only-its-share

Losing the foreground CLI ends that share alone; a background share continues.

Fixtures: signed in; one background share, then a foreground share whose CLI process dies.

```text
$ purlview share https://internal.example/demo --background
stderr| ✓ Sharing internal.example
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Opens    /demo · the whole app is reachable
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     purlview stop k7m2p4qx
= exit 0
$ purlview share localhost:3000
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://p4q9x2bd.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-02
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     Ctrl-C
        -- the CLI process running this command is killed (its daemon connection closes)
$ purlview list
stdout|   ID        APP               ACCESS                DEVICE       STATUS   EXPIRES
stdout| ● k7m2p4qx  internal.example  Anyone with the link  this device  Sharing  in 1h
= exit 0
```

## Background share

### background/returns-after-ready-and-is-manageable

A background share returns after the daemon owns it and the route is ready; later commands see and end it.

Fixtures: signed in.

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000 --background
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     purlview stop k7m2p4qx
= exit 0
$ purlview list
stdout|   ID        APP             ACCESS                DEVICE       STATUS   EXPIRES
stdout| ● k7m2p4qx  localhost:3000  Anyone with the link  this device  Sharing  in 1h
= exit 0
$ purlview link k7m2p4qx
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
= exit 0
$ purlview stop k7m2p4qx
stderr| ✓ Stopped k7m2p4qx — the link no longer works
= exit 0
$ purlview list
stderr| No active shares
stderr| → purlview share 3000
= exit 0
```

### background/lost-start-reply-is-reconciled

A lost start reply is retried with the same attempt id, so the daemon answers with the share it already owns.

Fixtures: signed in; the daemon receives the start but its reply is lost.

```text
        -- the daemon will receive the next start but the reply is lost
$ purlview share localhost:3000 --background
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     purlview stop k7m2p4qx
= exit 0
$ purlview list
stdout|   ID        APP             ACCESS                DEVICE       STATUS   EXPIRES
stdout| ● k7m2p4qx  localhost:3000  Anyone with the link  this device  Sharing  in 1h
= exit 0
```

### background/two-shares-same-target

Two intentional share commands for the same target create two shares; nothing is deduplicated by target.

Fixtures: signed in.

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000 --background
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     purlview stop k7m2p4qx
= exit 0
$ purlview share localhost:3000 --background
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://p4q9x2bd.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-02
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     purlview stop p4q9x2bd
= exit 0
$ purlview list
stdout|   ID        APP             ACCESS                DEVICE       STATUS   EXPIRES
stdout| ● k7m2p4qx  localhost:3000  Anyone with the link  this device  Sharing  in 1h
stdout| ● p4q9x2bd  localhost:3000  Anyone with the link  this device  Sharing  in 1h
= exit 0
```

## Share options

### options/short-ttl

--ttl requests a shorter lifetime; the share expires when it elapses.

Fixtures: signed in.

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000 --ttl 15m
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 15m · 12:15 PM
stderr| Stop     Ctrl-C
        -- clock advances (1m steps) until: Expires in 5 minutes
stderr|
stderr| 12:10 PM  ! Expires in 5 minutes
        -- clock +5m
stderr| 12:15 PM  Share expired
= exit 0
```

### options/invalid-ttl

An excessive or malformed --ttl is a usage error before anything starts.

Fixtures: signed in.

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000 --ttl 2h
stderr| ✗ --ttl 2h is over the 1h limit — use 1h or less
stderr| Run 'purlview share --help' for usage.
= exit 2
$ purlview share localhost:3000 --ttl abc
stderr| ✗ --ttl abc isn't a duration — use something like 15m
stderr| Run 'purlview share --help' for usage.
= exit 2
$ purlview share localhost:3000 --ttl 0
stderr| ✗ --ttl 0 is too short — use 1s or more
stderr| Run 'purlview share --help' for usage.
= exit 2
```

### options/invalid-target

What cannot be shared is a usage error that says what to type instead.

Fixtures: signed in.

```text
$ purlview share 70000
stderr| ✗ 70000 isn't a valid port — ports run from 1 to 65535
stderr| Run 'purlview share --help' for usage.
= exit 2
$ purlview share localhost
stderr| ✗ localhost needs a port — try purlview share localhost:3000
stderr| Run 'purlview share --help' for usage.
= exit 2
$ purlview share ftp://files.example:21
stderr| ✗ ftp addresses can't be shared — use http or https
stderr| Run 'purlview share --help' for usage.
= exit 2
$ purlview share http://admin:secret@localhost:3000
stderr| ✗ An address with a username or password can't be shared — remove them; your app's own login still applies
stderr| Run 'purlview share --help' for usage.
= exit 2
$ purlview share http://localhost:3000/app#top
stderr| ✗ The part after # never reaches an app — remove it
stderr| Run 'purlview share --help' for usage.
= exit 2
$ purlview share
```

## Connectivity

### connectivity/temporary-loss-and-reconnect

A dropped connection is announced, redocked after its back-off, and the same link and expiry continue.

Fixtures: signed in; the serving connection drops once.

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     Ctrl-C
        -- network: the serving connection drops
        -- clock advances (1s steps) until: Reconnected
stderr|
stderr| 12:00 PM  ! Connection lost — reconnecting
stderr| 12:00 PM  ✓ Reconnected — same link, still expires 1:00 PM
        -- clock +1h
stderr| 1:00 PM  ! Expires in 5 minutes
stderr| 1:00 PM  Share expired
= exit 0
```

### connectivity/platform-restart

A platform restart follows the same reconnect path with back-off; the share resumes with its original expiry.

Fixtures: signed in; the platform restarts (all connections drop, it is unreachable for a few seconds).

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     Ctrl-C
        -- platform restarts: connections drop, unreachable while it comes back
stderr|
stderr| 12:00 PM  ! Connection lost — reconnecting
        -- platform reachable again
        -- clock advances (1s steps) until: Reconnected
stderr| 12:00 PM  ✓ Reconnected — same link, still expires 1:00 PM
        -- Ctrl-C
stderr| 12:00 PM  ✓ Stopped — the link no longer works
= exit 0
```

### connectivity/expired-while-disconnected

A share the platform already expired is rejected on reconnect and ends as expired.

Fixtures: signed in; the connection drops and the platform expires the share before it reconnects.

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000 --ttl 15m
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 15m · 12:15 PM
stderr| Stop     Ctrl-C
        -- platform unreachable; the connection drops
stderr|
stderr| 12:00 PM  ! Connection lost — reconnecting
        -- the platform records the share as expired, then is reachable again
        -- clock advances (1s steps) until: Share expired
stderr| 12:00 PM  Share expired
= exit 0
```

### connectivity/revoked-while-disconnected

A share stopped elsewhere while disconnected is refused on reconnect and finishes as stopped from another device.

Fixtures: signed in; the connection drops; the share is stopped from the console.

```text

stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     Ctrl-C
        -- platform unreachable; the connection drops
stderr|

        -- the share is stopped from the console; the platform is reachable again
        -- clock advances (1s steps) until: Stopped from another device
stderr| 12:00 PM  Stopped from another device
= exit 0
```

### connectivity/invalid-authority-on-reconnect

A device that was signed out from elsewhere stops retrying and is told to sign in again (exit 1).

Fixtures: signed in; this device is signed out from the console while the connection is down.


### output/exit-status-classes

## link

### link/prints-only-the-link

link prints a share's link, and only that, for a share of any of your devices.

Fixtures: signed in; one background share here and one on the laptop.

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000 --background
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     purlview stop k7m2p4qx
= exit 0
$ purlview link k7m2p4qx
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
= exit 0
$ purlview link shr_p4q9x2bd
stdout| https://p4q9x2bd.purlview.invalid/
= exit 0
$ purlview link zzzzzzzz
stderr| ✗ No share zzzzzzzz in your account — see purlview list
= exit 1
$ purlview link
stderr| ✗ link needs a share id — see purlview list
stderr| Run 'purlview link --help' for usage.
= exit 2
        -- platform unreachable
$ purlview link k7m2p4qx
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
= exit 0
$ purlview link p4q9x2bd
stderr| ✗ Couldn't reach Purlview — check your connection and try again
= exit 1
```

```text
stderr| Stop     purlview stop p4q9x2bd
= exit 0
$ purlview share 8080 --background
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:8080
stderr|
stdout| https://f8q3w6hn.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-03
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     purlview stop f8q3w6hn
= exit 0
$ purlview stop k7m2p4qx
stderr| ✓ Stopped k7m2p4qx — the link no longer works
= exit 0
$ purlview stop https://p4q9x2bd.purlview-content.invalid/some/page?x=1
stderr| ✓ Stopped p4q9x2bd — the link no longer works
= exit 0
$ purlview unshare shr_f8q3w6hn
stderr| ✓ Stopped f8q3w6hn — the link no longer works
= exit 0
$ purlview list
stderr| No active shares
stderr| → purlview share 3000
= exit 0
```

### stop/local-foreground-share

stop from another terminal stops a foreground share; that terminal says it was stopped elsewhere and exits 0.

Fixtures: signed in; a foreground share runs in another terminal.

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     Ctrl-C
$ purlview stop k7m2p4qx
stderr| ✓ Stopped k7m2p4qx — the link no longer works
= exit 0
        (purlview share localhost:3000, continued)
stderr|
stderr| 12:00 PM  Stopped from another device
= exit 0
```

### stop/remote-device-share

stop stops a share of another device, connected or not; nothing waits for that device.

Fixtures: signed in; the laptop shares two apps; one has lost its connection.

```text
$ purlview stop k7m2p4qx
stderr| ✓ Stopped k7m2p4qx — the link no longer works
= exit 0
$ purlview stop p4q9x2bd
stderr| ✓ Stopped p4q9x2bd — the link no longer works
= exit 0
```

### stop/already-stopped

Stopping a share that was already stopped succeeds and says so.

Fixtures: signed in; a background share was stopped once already.

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000 --background
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     purlview stop k7m2p4qx
= exit 0
$ purlview stop k7m2p4qx
stderr| ✓ Stopped k7m2p4qx — the link no longer works
= exit 0
$ purlview stop k7m2p4qx
stderr| ✓ k7m2p4qx was already stopped
= exit 0
```

### stop/unknown-share

An unknown or someone else's share gets one line that tells them apart for nobody; what is not an id or a link is a usage error.

Fixtures: signed in.

```text
$ purlview stop zzzzzzzz
stderr| ✗ No share zzzzzzzz in your account — see purlview list
= exit 1
$ purlview stop 7K2M
stderr| ✗ 7K2M isn't a share id or link — see purlview list
stderr| Run 'purlview stop --help' for usage.
= exit 2
```

### stop/uncertain-confirmation

A stop whose confirmation is lost is reported as unconfirmed (exit 1); repeating it is safe.

Fixtures: signed in; one background share; the platform's acknowledgement is lost once.

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000 --background
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     purlview stop k7m2p4qx
= exit 0
        -- the platform's acknowledgement will be lost
$ purlview stop k7m2p4qx
stderr| ✗ Couldn't confirm k7m2p4qx stopped — try again, or see purlview list
= exit 1
$ purlview stop k7m2p4qx
stderr| ✓ k7m2p4qx was already stopped
= exit 0
```

### stop/purlview-unreachable-local-share

With Purlview unreachable, a share of this device stops here and the line says by when the link stops working (exit 1).

Fixtures: signed in; one background share; the platform is unreachable.

```text
$ purlview share localhost:3000 --background
stderr| ✓ Sharing localhost:3000
stderr|
stdout| https://k7m2p4qx.purlview.invalid/?token=synthetic-secret-01
stderr|
stderr| Access   Anyone with this link
stderr| Expires  in 1h · 1:00 PM
stderr| Stop     purlview stop k7m2p4qx
= exit 0
        -- platform unreachable
$ purlview stop k7m2p4qx
stderr| ! Stopped here, but Purlview couldn't confirm — the link stops working by 1:00 PM
= exit 1
```

### stop/purlview-unreachable-remote-share

With Purlview unreachable, another device's share cannot be stopped and nothing changes.

Fixtures: signed in; the laptop's share; the platform is unreachable.

```text
$ purlview stop k7m2p4qx
stderr| ✗ Couldn't reach Purlview — check your connection and try again
= exit 1
```

## devices

### devices/list

devices lists the devices signed in to the account; a dot marks this one.

Fixtures: signed in on this device today; the laptop signed in two weeks ago and shares one app.

```text
$ purlview devices
stdout|   NAME    SIGNED IN  LAST USED  SHARES
stdout|   laptop  Sep 2      today           1
stdout| ● studio  Sep 16     today           0
= exit 0
```

### devices/signout

devices signout asks first, naming what stops, and defaults to No; --yes skips the question.

Fixtures: signed in; the laptop shares one app.

```text
$ purlview devices signout laptop
stderr| Sign out laptop? Its 1 share will stop. [y/N]
        -- the user types: 
= exit 0
$ purlview devices signout laptop
stderr| Sign out laptop? Its 1 share will stop. [y/N]
        -- the user types: y
stderr| ✓ Signed out laptop
= exit 0
$ purlview devices signout laptop --yes
stderr| ✗ No device laptop in your account — see purlview devices
= exit 1
```

### devices/signout-refusals

devices signout refuses this device, a name two devices share, and a question nobody can answer.

Fixtures: signed in; two other devices are both named laptop.

```text
$ purlview devices signout studio --yes
stderr| ✗ studio is this device
stderr| → purlview logout
= exit 1
$ purlview devices signout laptop --yes
stderr| ✗ 2 devices are named laptop — sign one out by its id
stderr|   ID           SIGNED IN  LAST USED  SHARES
stderr|   dev_laptop   Sep 2      today           0
stderr|   dev_laptop2  Sep 15     Sep 15          0
= exit 1
$ purlview devices signout dev_laptop2
stderr| ✗ Signing out laptop needs a yes — add --yes
= exit 1
$ purlview devices signout dev_laptop2 --yes
stderr| ✓ Signed out laptop
= exit 0
```
